routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas plans sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, Tate categories, parity or Tate-parity sheaves, or tilting modules for a dual group in characteristic p, so a new roadmap is justified. The route now has 63 items. The review moved to it the Tate diagonal and the Frobenius twist of algebras (items 65, 66 and 68, the general form of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4), the constant term for the equal-characteristic Grassmannian (item 96, which GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans only for the B_dR^+ Grassmannian) and flatness over k[σ] for infinite modules (item 107, finite case only in Mathlib). It also added 18 items. The brief gained a corrections paragraph for Lemma 3.8, the proof of Lemma 4.14, Lemma 4.16 (false for the equivariant categories), the additivity of Psm∘Nm, Lemma 4.24 (true only on objects), the naturality gap in §A.4 and the composition order in §A.5.

The parent roadmap's coefficients are characteristic-zero ℓ-adic, and this paper's are k = F̄_p, so a Part II is right. The review found that the source route under-routes the modular side. The geometric L-group, both presentations of the excursion algebra, the modular reconstruction theorem (BHKT 4.5), homomorphisms of L-groups, the k-coefficient Satake functor on shtukas and Lemma B.5 are not planned with k-coefficients. They moved here as items 8, 11, 12, 13, 14, 53 and 104, with imports from LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2 for local Weil groups. The review also added 6 items, among them the semisimplicity of φ_BC∘ρ, which Theorems 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6 need, and the Exc^σ-action on Tate cohomology. The brief's corrections paragraph covers Lemma 2.7, (2.3), (2.1), the proof of Theorem 5.13 and Appendix B.

Mod p Bernstein centres at Moy–Prasad level, Z_TV and the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence are not planned; SR.3 is complex. The route had left open which of it and the Treumann–Venkatesh Part II owns the Brauer homomorphism, plain subgroups, linkage and the conjecture. The review settled it: SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality owns them, since it states them for any order-p automorphism, and this route imports them. Item 93 is planned by SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.6. The review added 7 missing items, among them tame Galois descent of Moy–Prasad filtrations and the mod p Bernstein centre as an inverse limit, split off item 70. It also added one library item, for Artin–Tate and Nakayama. The brief's corrections paragraph covers Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4 at r = 0, the missing Galois-fixed special vertex and Theorem 6.26 at r = 0.

The route is a source for GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands in its coefficient-independent geometric part, and only there. Its reason said that §2 is 'already planned', which is wrong for k-coefficients, so five items moved to route 2. The route keeps items 10, 52 and 54 and three new planned items (FWeil for GS.4, the ker¹ decomposition for GS.0 and HN truncations at deep level for GS.2). GS.0 is added to its layers.

notes:
The review is independent of the extraction, which was written by session cc-7b31c4. The reviewer, session cc-39fac3, earlier reviewed PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, which bears on the ownership decisions for routes 1 and 3, and says so here.

What was read: every item was checked against the published open-access text (Forum Math. Pi 12 (2024), e1) and the arXiv v6 TeX source, in five ranges by five checkers. Every formula relied on was checked on a page image. Cambridge Core lists no erratum or corrigendum, and v6 (29 November 2023) is the latest arXiv version, with the same text.

Corrections made in place: 55 statements (most add the standing hypotheses the extraction left out; others copy misprints of the paper, or are false as printed) and 15 locators. There are 15 status or routing changes and 35 new items (31 missing, 3 planned, 1 library), bringing the total to 142. Every missing item is routed once.

Source issues: E1–E7 are confirmed. E8–E57 are new: 33 misprints that affect nothing, and 17 other findings (one of them, E12, an error that affects nothing). The findings that matter:
- E9: Theorem 1.1 as printed omits the hypothesis that p is an odd good prime.
- E10, E11: Lemma 2.7 is false for general φ, and Theorems 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6 need φ_BC∘ρ semisimple. That is true, but not proved in the paper.
- E17: Lemma 3.8 needs bounded dimension.
- E25, E29: Lemmas 4.16 and 4.24 are false as printed. An independent adversarial check failed to refute either counterexample.
- E26, E27: the gaps in Lemma 4.14 and in the definition of BC^(p).
- E34: Theorem 4.20 is proved objectwise, but not as a natural isomorphism over Ĥ.
- E41: the proof of Theorem 5.13 misses the α-components.
- E46: Appendix B's partial-Frobenius inverses.
- E48–E50: Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4 are false at r = 0, and the Galois-fixed special vertex need not exist (SL_1(D)). Both are repaired at r > 0 at any point of B(H/F_v), which also completes the proof of Theorem 6.26.
- E51: Theorem 6.26 at r = 0 is unproved.
Theorems 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, and Theorem 1.1 for p odd and good, stand with the repairs recorded. Theorem 4.20, as a natural isomorphism of functors, rests on the open step E34, and Proposition 5.12(i) on E29.
